title: Backend Engineering
tagline: Server runtimes, distributed systems, resilient APIs, and data architecture
description: Master server-side architectures from low-level networking and HTTP protocols to transactional databases, caching layers, authentication protocols, and high-throughput event queues.
prerequisites: Programming foundations in one language (JS/TS, Go, Python, Java)

stages.title: Stage 1: Networking & API Protocols
stages.description: Deep dive into OSI model, TCP/UDP, TLS handshakes, HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3, and modern API protocols.

nodes.title: HTTP Internals, Status Codes & Idempotency
nodes.description: How client-server communication functions over TCP/TLS: request headers, response codes, connection pooling, and idempotent method semantics.
nodes.whyItMatters: Non-idempotent endpoints cause duplicate payments or inventory deductions on network retries. Correct status codes allow CDNs and clients to handle caching and errors properly.
keyTakeaways: GET, PUT, and DELETE methods must be idempotent; POST is non-idempotent.
Use Idempotency-Key headers in payment and mutation APIs to safely deduplicate retries.
Choose between 401 Unauthorized (unauthenticated) and 403 Forbidden (authenticated but not permitted).
nodes.interviewTips: Be ready to explain what happens at the network layer during an HTTPS TLS 1.3 handshake and TCP 3-way handshake.

nodes.title: API Architectures: REST vs gRPC vs GraphQL
nodes.description: Evaluating API communication paradigms: JSON-over-HTTP REST, binary Protocol Buffers over HTTP/2 with gRPC, and client-specified GraphQL queries.
nodes.whyItMatters: Internal microservices communicating via heavy JSON text create substantial serialization overhead. gRPC provides compact binary serialization and bi-directional streaming.
keyTakeaways: Use REST/JSON for public-facing developer APIs where universal tooling and human readability matter.
Use gRPC for high-throughput, low-latency east-west internal microservice communication.
Use Protocol Buffers schema definitions as the single source of truth for cross-language contracts.
nodes.interviewTips: Interviewers frequently ask you to design an API schema and discuss tradeoffs between REST over-fetching and GraphQL query-complexity Denial of Service risks.

stages.title: Stage 2: Database Storage & Query Optimization
stages.description: Relational data modeling, ACID transaction guarantees, isolation levels, indexing strategies, and connection pooling.

nodes.title: PostgreSQL Internals, B-Trees & Indexing
nodes.description: How relational storage engines store pages on disk, navigate B-Tree indexes, and execute query plans via EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
nodes.whyItMatters: Unindexed table scans degrade from milliseconds to minutes as tables grow to millions of rows, locking database CPU and crashing applications.

resources.title: Use The Index, Luke (SQL Indexing Guide)

keyTakeaways: Composite indexes must follow the Leftmost Prefix rule to match query WHERE clauses.
Avoid indexing columns with low selectivity (like boolean flags) unless using partial indexes.
Always inspect EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) to verify if an index scan or sequential scan is used.
nodes.interviewTips: You will be asked to explain how a B-Tree operates, what a covering index is, and why `SELECT *` hurts performance.

nodes.title: ACID Transactions & Isolation Levels
nodes.description: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability: Dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, phantom reads, and Serializable isolation.
nodes.whyItMatters: Concurrent balance updates or seat reservations without proper transaction isolation cause race conditions and financial double-spending.
keyTakeaways: Default isolation in PostgreSQL is Read Committed; it prevents dirty reads but allows non-repeatable reads.
Use optimistic locking (version column) or `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` (pessimistic locking) to prevent lost updates.
Keep transactions as short as possible to prevent connection pool exhaustion and lock contention.
nodes.interviewTips: Be prepared to explain the difference between Read Committed and Serializable isolation levels and write a deadlock-free concurrent update.

stages.title: Stage 3: Caching, Queues & Asynchronous Jobs
stages.description: Redis data structures, caching topologies, cache invalidation, and asynchronous job processing with message brokers.

nodes.title: Distributed Caching Strategies with Redis
nodes.description: Cache-aside, write-through, write-behind patterns, TTL expiration, cache stampede prevention, and Redis data primitives.
nodes.whyItMatters: Sub-millisecond in-memory caches protect primary databases from overwhelming read spikes during traffic surges.
keyTakeaways: Cache-aside pattern: application reads from cache; on miss, reads from DB and writes to cache with TTL.
Prevent cache stampedes (thundering herd) with distributed mutex locks or probabilistic early expiration.
Add jitter (random offset) to cache expiration times so thousands of keys don't expire in the same second.
nodes.interviewTips: Classic interview topic: how to handle cache penetration, cache breakdown, and cache avalanche.

nodes.title: Event-Driven Queues & Kafka/RabbitMQ
nodes.description: Decoupling workloads with asynchronous message queues: point-to-point brokers (RabbitMQ) vs distributed commit logs (Apache Kafka).
nodes.whyItMatters: Synchronous HTTP calls between services create cascading failures. Message queues provide backpressure and reliable delivery.
keyTakeaways: RabbitMQ pushes messages to consumers and deletes upon ack; Kafka is an append-only distributed log with consumer offsets.
Design consumers to be idempotent to safely handle at-least-once message delivery guarantees.
Implement Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) to quarantine unprocessable messages without halting the pipeline.
nodes.interviewTips: Expect questions comparing push vs pull queue models and explaining how Kafka consumer groups distribute partition reading.

stages.title: Stage 4: Auth, Resilience & Production Operations
stages.description: OAuth 2.1, OIDC, JWT security, circuit breakers, rate limiting, and observability.

nodes.title: Authentication, OAuth2 & JWT Security
nodes.description: Password hashing with Argon2/Bcrypt, session cookies vs stateless JWTs, OAuth 2.1 Authorization Code with PKCE, and RBAC.
nodes.whyItMatters: Flawed authentication architecture leads to token forgery, broken access controls (IDOR), and catastrophic data breaches.
keyTakeaways: Never roll custom cryptographic algorithms; use Argon2id for password hashing.
Short-lived access tokens (15m) paired with rotating refresh tokens mitigate stolen token replay risks.
Always enforce authorization checks on the server by verifying resource ownership against the authenticated subject.
nodes.interviewTips: Be prepared to explain how to safely revoke JWTs and how OAuth 2.0 PKCE flow works for single-page apps and mobile clients.
